en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 3.3.
Cūḷantaraduka, Kusalattika (The Lesser Intermediate Dyads, Wholesome Triads)
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.
Dependent on a conditioned wholesome state, a conditioned wholesome state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: one; in the case of object condition: one; in the case of predominance condition: one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a wholesome state with conditions, a wholesome state with conditions arises by way of the non-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.)

One [condition] by way of not-predominance; one by way of not-prenascence; one by way of not-postnascence; one by way of not-repetition; one by way of not-kamma; one by way of not-resultant; one by way of not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.
The sections on conascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence (*paṭicca*). Root-condition (*hetu*).
A conditioned wholesome state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a conditioned wholesome state. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of root;
one in the case of object … pe … one in the case of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a conditioned unwholesome state, a conditioned unwholesome state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, one; in the case of object condition, one …pe… in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. (Also in the section on co-nascence …pe… and in the section on inquiry, it is one in every instance. 3.3.1.2.
Indeterminate Section 3.3.1.2.1–7. Section on Dependent, etc.
The Tetrad of Conditions:
Root.
Dependent upon a conditioned indeterminate state, a conditioned indeterminate state arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: one; in the case of object condition: one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition:
one. (Abbreviated. In the case of not-root: one; in the case of not-object: one; in the case of not-predominance: one. (In all cases: one; abbreviated. Root, etc.
A conditioned indeterminate state is a condition for a conditioned indeterminate state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
A conditioned indeterminate state is a condition for a conditioned indeterminate state by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).
An unconditioned indeterminate state is a condition for a conditioned indeterminate state by way of the object-condition.
A conditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for a conditioned indeterminate state.
An unconditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for a conditioned indeterminate state—as object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*).

(Abbreviated. In the case of root condition (*hetu*): one; in the case of object condition (*ārammaṇa*): two; in the case of predominance condition (*adhipati*): two; in the case of proximity condition (*anantara*): one …pe… in the case of dependence condition (*nissaya*): one; in the case of decisive support condition (*upanissaya*): two; in the case of prenascence condition (*purejāta*): one; in the case of postnascence condition (*pacchājāta*): one (in all cases: one); in the case of non-disappearance condition (*avigata*): one. (Abbreviated.)

A conditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for a conditioned indeterminate state; it is a condition by way of conascence-condition (*sahajātapaccaya*); it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).
An unconditioned indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a conditioned indeterminate state; it is a condition by way of decisive support-condition. (Abbreviated.)
Two by way of not-root condition; one by way of not-object condition. (Abbreviated.
One by way of root condition and not-object condition. (Abbreviated.
Two by way of not-root condition and object condition. (Abbreviated.)
The "Conditioned Dyad" and "Wholesome Triad" are completed.
3.3.2. Conditioned Dyad, Wholesome Triad:
Dependent on a conditioned wholesome state, a conditioned wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
The Duality of the Conditioned and the Triplet of the Wholesome is finished.
3.3.3. The Duality of the Visible and the Triplet of the Wholesome. 3.3.3.1.
The Section on the Wholesome.
3.3.3.1.1–7 Section on "Dependent" and Other Terms (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on a non-demonstrable wholesome state, a non-demonstrable wholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One for root;
one for object ... pe ... one for non-disappearance. (In the "Conascent" section ... pe ... and in the "Investigation" section, it is one in all cases. 3.3.3.2. Unwholesome Section.
3.3.3.2.1–7 Section on "Dependent" and Other Terms (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions— Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on an invisible unwholesome state, an invisible unwholesome state arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root, one; under object, one … pe … under non-disappearance, one. (In the section on co-nascence … pe … and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all cases. 3.3.3.3.
The Indeterminate Section.
3.3.3.3.1–7 Section on "Dependent on" and so forth (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka) – Root Condition (Hetu)
Dependent on a non-indicative, indeterminate state, a non-indicative, indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: one; under predominance: three ... pe ... under non-disappearance:

three. (Abbreviated. Under not-root: three (three in all cases); under not-kamma: three; under not-resultant: three; under not-nutriment: three ... pe ... under not-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
Root, etc.:
A non-manifest, indeterminate state is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a non-manifest, indeterminate state... [three].
A visible indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-visible indeterminate state.
A non-visible indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a non-visible indeterminate state.
A visible indeterminate state is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a non-visible indeterminate state—namely, as an object-predominance.
A non-demonstrable indeterminate state is a condition for a non-demonstrable indeterminate state by way of predominance-condition:

as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. A non-demonstrable indeterminate state is a condition for both a demonstrable indeterminate state and a non-demonstrable indeterminate state by way of predominance-condition: as conascence-predominance.
A visible indeterminate state is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for an invisible indeterminate state—namely, natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).

An invisible indeterminate state is a condition, by way of decisive support condition, for an invisible indeterminate state—namely, object decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*) … [abbreviated] … Under root condition there are three;

under object condition there are two; under predominance condition there are three; under proximity condition there is one … [abbreviated] … under conascence condition there are three; under mutuality condition … [abbreviated] … *Note: The text provided ends abruptly with "aññamaññe". The full list of conditions would typically continue with "nissaye tīṇi, sampayutte tīṇi, vippayutte tīṇi, atthiyā tīṇi, natthiyā ekaṃ, vigate ekaṃ, avigate tīṇi."*
One [condition] in dependence; three in support; two in decisive support; three in prenascence; three in postnascence;
one in repetition; three in kamma; three in result (three in all cases); one in association; three in dissociation; five in presence;
one in absence …pe… five in non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)
The "Visible Pair" and the "Wholesome Triplet" are completed.
Neither the "Conditionless," nor the "Unconditioned," nor the "Visible" is found [in this context].
3.3.4. The "Impinging Pair" and the "Wholesome Triplet."
3.3.4.1. Section on the Wholesome (Kusalapada) 3.3.4.1.1–6: The Chapter on "Dependent Upon" Etc. (Paṭiccādivāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccayacatukka)
Dependent on a non-reactive wholesome state, a non-reactive wholesome state arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Under root-condition there is one; under object-condition there is one … pe … under dissociation-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there is one. (Abbreviated.)
(In the section on co-nascence, ...pe... and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all cases.
Dependent on a non-reacting unwholesome state, a non-reacting unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
It is one in the case of root; ...pe... it is one in the case of non-disappearance (and in the section on inquiry, it is one in all cases).
3.3.4.2. Indeterminate Section (Abyākata-pada) 3.3.4.2.1–6. The Chapter on "Dependent on," etc. (Paṭicca-ādi-vāra):
The Tetrad of Conditions (Paccaya-catukka)
Dependent on a state that is impinging and indeterminate, an impinging indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is impinging and indeterminate, a non-impinging indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a reactive indeterminate state, both a reactive indeterminate state and a non-reactive indeterminate state arise by way of root condition... [nine].
Dependent on a non-reactive indeterminate state, a non-reactive indeterminate state arises by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root-cause condition, there are nine; in object condition, one; in predominance condition, nine ... [and so on] ... in mutuality condition, six; in support condition, nine; in decisive support condition, one; in prenascence and repetition conditions, one; in kamma condition, nine; in resultant condition, nine ... [and so on] ... in non-disappearance condition, nine. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a state that is not-root, impinging, and indeterminate, there arises a state that is impinging and indeterminate by way of the not-root condition. (Abbreviated.)
Nine by way of not-root … pe … nine by way of not-disappearance. (In all cases there are nine; abbreviated.
3.3.4.1.7. Chapter on Questions:
The Tetrad of Conditions.
A non-reactive, indeterminate state is a condition for a non-reactive, indeterminate state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). (Abbreviated.

There are three [conditions] in the case of the root, two in the case of the object, three in the case of the predominance, one in the case of the immediate, one in the case of the contiguous, and one in the case of the conascent.
Nine [ways] by way of mutuality, six by way of reciprocity, nine by way of dependence, two by way of decisive support, three by way of prenascence,
three by way of postnascence, one by way of repetition, three by way of kamma, three by way of result, three by way of nutriment, five by way of faculty, three by way of jhāna, three by way of path,
one by way of association, four by way of dissociation, nine by way of presence, one by way of absence, one by way of disappearance, and nine by way of non-disappearance.
The resistant indeterminate state is a condition for the resistant indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine [conditions] are excluded from the root-cause; nine are excluded from the object-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: two. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)
The Section on the Pair of the Impinging and the Triplet of the Wholesome is finished.
3.3.5. The Pair of the Material and the Triplet of the Wholesome:
Root.
Dependent on an immaterial wholesome state, an immaterial wholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
One [condition] in the case of the root; one in the case of the object.
Dependent on an immaterial unwholesome state, an immaterial unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition, one; in the case of object condition, one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition, one. Root and Object:
Dependent on a material indeterminate state, a material indeterminate state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a non-material indeterminate state, a non-material indeterminate state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on both a material indeterminate state and a non-material indeterminate state, a material indeterminate state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on a material indeterminate state, a non-material indeterminate state arises by way of object condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause: nine; with respect to object: three; with respect to predominance: five; with respect to proximity: three; with respect to contiguity: three …pe… with respect to mutuality:

six …pe… with respect to prenascence: one; with respect to repetition: one; with respect to kamma: nine; with respect to result: nine …pe… with respect to non-disappearance: nine. (Abbreviated. With respect to not-cause: nine;
with respect to not-object: three; with respect to not-predominance: nine …pe… with respect to not-prenascence: nine …pe… with respect to not-kamma: [nine].
Two [factors] are not resultant; five are not nutriment; one is not faculty; two are not jhāna; nine are not path; three are not associated;
two are not dissociated; three are not absent; three are not disappeared. (Abbreviated; the negative [converse]). Root.
A non-material indeterminate state is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a non-material indeterminate state.

(Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there are three; under the object-condition, two; under the predominance-condition, three; under the proximity-condition, one; under the contiguity-condition, one;

under the conascence-condition, seven; under the mutuality-condition, six; under the dependence-condition, seven; under the strong-dependence-condition, two; under the prenascence-condition, one; under the postnascence-condition, one.
In the case of repetition, one; in karma, three; in result, three; in nutriment, four; in faculty, six; in jhāna, three; in path, three; in association, one;
in dissociation, two ... [and so on] ... in non-disappearance, seven. (Abbreviated. In the absence of root, seven;
in the absence of object, seven. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: two. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive methods were calculated for the Question Section of the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.)
The Triplet on the Wholesome of the Form Realm is finished.
3.3.6. The Worldly Dyad, the Wholesome Triplet:
Root.
Dependent on a mundane wholesome state, a mundane wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a supramundane wholesome state, a supramundane wholesome state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a mundane wholesome state, a mundane wholesome state arises by way of object condition.
Dependent on supramundane wholesome state, arises supramundane wholesome state by object condition. (Abbreviated.
Two for root, two for object, two for predominance … pe … two for kamma … pe … two for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated; Positive.
Two for not-predominance … pe … one for not-repetition … pe … two for not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
A mundane wholesome state, such as a root-cause and so forth, is a condition for a mundane wholesome state by way of the root-cause condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
Supramundane wholesome state is a condition for supramundane wholesome state by way of root-condition.
Mundane wholesome state is a condition for mundane wholesome state by way of object-condition.
Supramundane wholesome state is a condition for mundane wholesome state by way of object-condition.
A mundane wholesome state is a condition for a mundane wholesome state by way of predominance condition: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance.
A supramundane wholesome state is a condition for a supramundane wholesome state by way of predominance condition: as conascence-predominance.
A supramundane wholesome state is a condition for a mundane wholesome state by way of predominance condition: as object-predominance. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition, there are two; in the object condition, two; in the predominance condition, three; in the proximity condition, two; in the contiguity condition, two; in the conascence condition, two …pe… in the decisive support condition, four; in the repetition condition, two; in the kamma condition, two; in the nutriment condition, two …pe… in the non-disappearance condition, two. (Abbreviated.
Dependent on a mundane unwholesome state, a mundane unwholesome state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

In the case of root condition: one; in the case of object condition: one … pe … in the case of non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated; the section on conascence and the section on inquiry are identical in all respects.
Root:
Dependent on a mundane indeterminate state, a mundane indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a supramundane indeterminate state, a supramundane indeterminate state arises by way of root condition … three.
Dependent on both a mundane indeterminate and a supramundane indeterminate state, a mundane indeterminate state arises by way of root condition.

(Abbreviated. Under root condition there are five; under object condition, two … pe … under repetition condition, one; under kamma condition, five; under resultant condition, five … pe … under non-disappearance condition, five. (Abbreviated; positive sequence.)
By way of not-root: one; by way of not-object: three; by way of not-predominance: two …pe… by way of not-prenascence:
four; by way of not-postnascence: five …pe… by way of not-kamma: one; by way of not-resultant: one; by way of not-nutriment: one …pe… by way of not-path:
one; by way of not-association: three; by way of not-dissociation: two; by way of not-absence: three; by way of not-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated; the Negative.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
A mundane indeterminate state is a condition for a mundane indeterminate state by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).
A supramundane indeterminate state is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a supramundane indeterminate state … three.
(Abbreviated. Under root: four; under object: three; under predominance: four; under proximity: four; under conascence: five; under mutuality: two;
under dependence: seven; under strong-dependence: four; under prenascence: two; under postnascence: two; under repetition: [four].

One [condition], four in the case of karma, four in the case of result, four in the case of nutriment … pe … four in the case of the path, two in the case of association, three in the case of dissociation, seven in the case of presence … pe … seven in the case of non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the section on questions in the *Kusala-ttika*, so too should they be calculated here.)
The Worldly Twofold on Wholesome States is finished.
3.3.7. The Twofold on Cognizable by Something, the Triplet on Wholesome States, and the Root [Triplet].
Dependent on a wholesome state cognizable by some, a wholesome state cognizable by some arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state cognizable by some, a wholesome state not cognizable by anyone arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a wholesome state cognizable by some, a wholesome state cognizable by some...
And by some [condition] it is not cognizable; yet wholesome states arise with root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Nine for root, nine for object … pe … nine for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
Negative (Paccanīya).
Conditioned by a wholesome state cognizable by anyone, a wholesome state cognizable by anyone arises by way of the not-predominance condition. (Abbreviated. Nine [ways] for not-predominance;
nine for not-prenascence; nine for not-postnascence; nine for not-repetition; nine for not-kamma; nine for not-resultant ... pe ... nine for not-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, conditionality, support, association, and conjunction should be expanded in the same manner as the section on dependence.
Root Condition: A wholesome state cognizable by someone is a condition, by way of root condition, for a wholesome state cognizable by someone. (Abbreviated.)

With root condition: nine; with object condition: nine; with predominance condition: nine; with proximity condition: nine; with contiguity condition: nine … pe … with kamma condition: nine … pe … with non-disappearance condition: nine. (Abbreviated. Without root condition: nine;
without object condition: nine. (Abbreviated. With root condition, without object condition: nine. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object [condition]. (Abbreviated.
(Just as the positive, negative, positive-negative, and negative-positive enumerations were calculated for the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet, so should they be calculated here.
That which is cognizable by some is unwholesome, and that which is cognizable by some is indeterminate.)
It should be expanded in detail like the "knowable-by-some-wholesome" [tetrad].
The "wholesome triad of the knowable-by-some-dyad" is finished.
The "Minor Intermediate Dyad" is finished.
